About Us
Introduction
Acorn Intervention Centre caters for children from 2 years to Reception who have been identified as having SEND. Referrals into the centre can be done by parents or your early years provider by contacting the school.
OAKLEIGH SCHOOL & THE EARLY YEARS INTERVENTION CENTRE caters for children aged 5-11 years who have severe learning difficulties and complex needs. The population includes children with additional needs, such as physical or sensory, and autism.
Admissions
Children who come to Oakleigh school have an Education, Health and Care Plan where the Local Authority has named our school. To arrange a visit, please call the school office on 0208 368 5336, option 0. Please see our Admissions Policy.
For Acorn admissions please see our Early Years section.
School Organisation
Oakleigh School provides for children who have severe and complex learning difficulties. Classes are organised within the key stages (in exceptional circumstances this may change) and children are grouped in order to deliver outstanding teaching strategies to meet their needs. From September 2022 the school expanded to have a satellite provision based at Queenswell School.
Oakleigh has a large staff team comprising skilled and committed teachers, learning support assistants, mealtime supervisors, site manager, administrative staff and ICT support who are fully supported by a range of other professionals (see Therapists and Health, Family Support Team). The multidisciplinary team all work together to ensure the very best outcomes are met for all our children.
Acorn Assessment Centre Organisational Chart September 2022.pptx
Oakleigh at Queenswell Organisational Chart 2022.pptx
Oakleigh Leadership Structure 2022-23.pptx
Inclusion
Children may visit local school supported by Oakleigh staff and we also welcome our mainstream peers into school for positive inclusion opportunities with the wider community.

Welcome
WELCOME TO OAKLEIGH SCHOOL AND THE ACORN ASSESSMENT CENTRE
A very warm welcome to Oakleigh School, where our motto 'Being the best we can be' reflects our unwavering commitment to each child's personal growth and success. We are a primary maintained special school in the Local Authority of Barnet for children which caters for pupils with a wide range of complex and profound learning difficulties. These include severe autism, complex medical conditions, physical and mobility difficulties, as well as severe developmental delay.
Our skilled and dedicated staff team work very hard to ensure learning is challenging, fun and engaging whilst ensuring that our pupils feel safe, valued and self-confident. We work effectively with our extended network of therapists, NHS colleagues, and other professionals to best support and meet the needs of our pupils.
We are proud of the strong partnerships we have built with families and the wider community, and we see these connections as key to creating the best possible learning experience. Together, we help our pupils grow in confidence and resilience, preparing them for the next phase in their lives whilst having the best opportunities to be happy and fulfilled.
If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact the school office via e-mail or telephone.
CLARE POWER Headteacher at Oakleigh School

PE and Sport Premium
We have developed different areas of our playground to include a range of colourful and motivating floor markings. This has enable us to extend outside learning opportunities for the children, both during structured lessons and play times, through motivating resources.
The floor markings have increased learning opportunities for the children, combined with promoting the development of physical skills. The floor markings include an alphabet train, a caterpillar with numbers, a target throwing game 1-20, 4 way hop scotch, snake letters, rocket hopscotch, alphabet shapes and a custom road in the ball court.

Early Years SEND Advisory Team
Early Years SEND Advisory Team
EARLY YEARS SPECIAL EDUCATIONAL NEEDS AND DISABILITY ADVISORY TEAM
Our role is to support children under 5 who live in Barnet who are likely to have Special Educational Needs (SEN). We support children at home and in their early years settings until they start at a maintained school setting. We fulfil the statutory role of the Area SENCo.
Our role includes supporting Barnet’s private, voluntary and independent (PVI) early years settings (who take Government funding) and Child-minding Quality and Support Officers who support all child minding settings. The Team work to promote inclusive learning environments and to support, up skill and empower Early Years Setting SENCOs to carry out their role and duties.
Barnet Early Years SEND Advisory Team Intervention Pathways
We aim to work together with parents, carers and early years settings, to help children make developmental progress.
Head of Service - Joann Moore
Deputy Head of Service - Trish Moysey

The documents in this section are intended to support you in your role as setting SENCO. The SENCO TOOLKIT contains ideas and guides for various aspects of your role from explaining what a setting SENCO does, how to advise and support your colleagues in helping children to learn, meeting with parents when you have concerns and many others.
